summary: Episode ep_002 (EP=ep_002, scene sc_001, 0-110000 ms, cathedral) shows Juliana publicly rejected at the altar by Gerald, who chooses Clarissa, and then rebuked by her father, Clarissa and a matriarch before she turns the humiliation into a public accusation against Gerald. Only the EP02:E1-EP02:E74 event text is treated as on-screen evidence. The metadata logline and continuity note, including the claim that this picks up from Episode 1's cliffhanger, are unverified and not used as evidence. Identities are uncertain: Gerald is inferred from camera directions naming him, Clarissa from E33 and E2, and the speaker labelled THE FORMER GROOM is taken as Gerald. The father is seen in E22-E27 but the BLOND NOBLEMAN speaker at E28 and E30 is only probably him, and the matriarch's off-screen voice at E48 and E50 is not confirmed as hers. Several speaker tags are malformed (for example '[Off-screen)'), and the tags were read as off-screen indicators without altering the dialogue. Juliana's claims about Clarissa's promises and Gerald's prior word are her own assertions and are not verified by on-screen events.

characters.role: Jilted bride and protagonist; speaks as LADY JULIANA; addressed as sister by Clarissa in EP02:E34

characters.name: Gerald
characters.role: Former groom who publicly rejects Juliana for Clarissa; speaks as THE FORMER GROOM

characters.name: Clarissa
characters.role: Juliana's sister who marries Gerald's place at the altar; speaks as LADY IN GOLD GOWN

characters.name: Father (unnamed)
characters.role: Juliana's father in the family pew who sides against her; identity as BLOND NOBLEMAN speaker is uncertain

characters.name: Matriarch (unnamed)
characters.role: Black-velvet-gowned older woman who scolds Juliana; off-screen voice attribution uncertain

beats.description: Gerald, at the altar steps with Clarissa behind him, tells Juliana he cannot marry her.
Gerald insults Juliana as plain, silent and beneath him while Clarissa smiles at him.
Juliana steps forward and pleads with Gerald, reminding him of his word before both families; he remains cold and unmoved.
Gerald says promises change when a better choice appears and that Clarissa is what he should have chosen from the start.
Juliana appeals to her father in the family pew, who refuses to intervene and tells her to accept it and not disgrace them further.
Clarissa mocks Juliana's gown, appearance and dead mother's apothecary, while Juliana's tearful expression hardens into indignation.
A matriarch in black velvet confronts Juliana in the aisle and tells her to be grateful she is allowed to attend.
Gerald gestures Juliana toward the exit and tells her to go home with some dignity; she turns back toward the altar.

Juliana's pain turns into a defiant smile; she stands tall, accuses Gerald of abandoning a woman who trusted him for a promise of beauty and wealth, and warns him not to mistake her heartbreak for his victory.

Juliana tells the congregation that Gerald's conduct has shown them what his word is worth, leaves Gerald frozen, and closes with a proud statement that she will not leave believing she should be ashamed.

revelations.claim: Gerald says he has replaced Juliana with Clarissa as a better choice, implying he now prefers her.
